File: src/config.ts

In the int() helper, Number.parseInt silently truncates trailing non-numeric characters (e.g. "12h" -> 12) instead of rejecting the value; it should validate that the entire string is a valid integer (e.g. using Number() with Number.isInteger, or checking for leftover characters) and throw for values like "12h" or "1h" so misconfigured TOKEN_TTL_MINUTES/RESET_TOKEN_TTL_MINUTES fail startup instead of being silently misread.

label: bug
file: src/config.ts
This comment was written by RepoMind, an automated triage agent. To reach a person, mention @ledgerline/maintainers.
src/config.ts's int() function does `Number.parseInt(raw, 10)` and only checks Number.isNaN(value); parseInt("12h",10) returns 12 without NaN, so TOKEN_TTL_MINUTES=12h becomes tokenTtlMinutes=60*... actually 12, matching the reported expiresInMinutes: 12, and the service starts without complaint as the reporter observed.

input.body:
File: src/api/health.ts

The handler only returns a non-200 status (503) when status is "down"; a "degraded" status (e.g. queue depth over QUEUE_DEGRADED_AT) still yields HTTP 200, so a simple load-balancer probe watching the status code can't detect degradation. The status-to-HTTP-code mapping should be changed so "degraded" also returns a non-200 code (or the runbook/docs should clearly specify that only the JSON body, not the HTTP code, signals degraded, if that is intentional).

label: bug
file: src/api/health.ts
This comment was written by RepoMind, an automated triage agent. To reach a person, mention @ledgerline/maintainers.
src/api/health.ts: `res.status(status === "down" ? 503 : 200).json({...})` means status "degraded" (set when checks.queue === "degraded") still responds with HTTP 200, matching the exact symptom in the issue.

input.title: Add an optional name/search query parameter to the GET /reports handler
input.body:
File: src/api/reports.ts

Add an optional name/search query parameter to the GET /reports handler (and pass it through to reportRepo.list / its SQL query in src/db/repos/reportRepo.ts) so the reports list can be filtered by name instead of only paginated.

label: feature
file: src/api/reports.ts
This comment was written by RepoMind, an automated triage agent. To reach a person, mention @ledgerline/maintainers.
src/api/reports.ts's GET /reports handler only calls parsePage() and reportRepo.list(userId, pageSize, offset) with no filter argument, and reportRepo.list(userId, limit, offset) in src/db/repos/reportRepo.ts takes no name/search parameter, confirming there is currently no way to filter the 340 saved reports by name as requested.

File: docs/API.md

In the Auth table/row for POST /auth/password-reset/confirm, document the password validation rule (minimum 10, maximum 200 characters, per src/api/auth.ts's zod schema) so the 400 'validation failed' response is explained.

label: docs
file: docs/API.md
This comment was written by RepoMind, an automated triage agent. To reach a person, mention @ledgerline/maintainers.
docs/API.md describes the confirm endpoint body as `{ token, password }` with no mention of password requirements, while src/api/auth.ts line 37 enforces `password: z.string().min(10).max(200)`, which is the undocumented rule the reporter hit.

input.title: pickLocale() should parse and sort by the q weight (defaulting to 1.0 wh
input.body:
File: src/i18n/index.ts

pickLocale() should parse and sort by the q weight (defaulting to 1.0 when absent) instead of taking the first entry in header order, so that e.g. 'en;q=0.3, fr-FR;q=0.9' resolves to 'fr'.

label: bug
file: src/i18n/index.ts
This comment was written by RepoMind, an automated triage agent. To reach a person, mention @ledgerline/maintainers.
src/i18n/index.ts's pickLocale iterates header.split(',') in order and returns the first part's language code that isLocale() recognizes, never reading or comparing the ';q=' value, which matches the reported behavior of ignoring q weights and picking the first listed (English) language.
